question: to the Commission Ciaran Mullooly (Renew) Subject:

Healthcare and social care workers who contracted COVID-19 at work continue to experience Long Covid, with severe impacts on their health, work capacity and financial security. In its resolution on the COVID-19 pandemic: lessons learned and recommendations for the future, the European Parliament called on EU countries to provide adequate support to people suffering from Long Covid, including by extending sickness allowances and facilitating access to social benefit schemes, and called for the recognition of Long Covid as an occupational disease for those workers. In this context and in view of the situation of healthcare workers who have exhausted sickness benefits and face a sudden drop in income while still unfit for work: What assessment has the Commission made of the extent to which Member States are giving practical effect to Parliament’s 2023 recommendations on adequate support for people with Long Covid, including access to sickness allowances and social protection schemes?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.8.2026) The design and management of social protection systems, including eligibility to sickness benefits and their duration, remains fundamentally the responsibility of the Member States (Article 153 (4) Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union). The Commission supports Member States through facilitating exchange of experience, analysis and policy guidance. The summary report of the 2024 mutual learning on access to social protection1 with focus on health, sickness, accidents at work and occupational diseases shows that most measures implemented as a response to the COVID-19 pandemic were only temporary and, in some cases, structural reforms were postponed. The Commission Recommendation (EU) 2022/2337 calls on Member States to recognise COVID-19 as an occupational disease, including when caused by work in health and social care2. Eurostat’s survey on the possibility of recognising COVID-19 as being of occupational origin3 shows that, in most countries, COVID-19 can be linked to work-related activities. However, the form of recognition varies between countries. The Commission recognises the significant medical and socioeconomic consequences of Long COVID and remains committed to supporting effective responses across these areas. The Network of Expertise on Long COVID4, supported from the EU4Health programme5 and carried out in collaboration with international organisations, aims to strengthen EU and national-level responses, including a training programme for healthcare professionals.
